text: If you dropped Mount Everest into the deepest part of the ocean, it would disappear.
This is the Mariana Trench, in the western Pacific.
Everest stands eight thousand eight hundred and forty-nine metres tall.
The bottom of the trench, the Challenger Deep, is almost eleven thousand metres down.
So its summit would still sit more than two kilometres under water.
The trench is over two and a half thousand kilometres long. Roughly London to Moscow.
At the bottom, eight tons press on every square inch.
And yet, things live down there. Tiny shrimp-like animals called amphipods.
Humans first reached the bottom in 1960. Just two men.
Even today, far more people have been to space than to the bottom of this trench.
